title: 1to1 prep: API + Console sync (Ryan)
content:
Quick goal: hit this 30m with clear asks and 3 concrete next steps. Save the parking-lot items for async follow-up.

Agenda (20–30m):
- Quick status: Hosted API perf regression (2–3 min)
- Console rollout: canary results + fallout (5–7 min)
- Dedicated capacity: customer quota/overprovision ask (5 min)
- Private deployment onboarding: checklist gaps (5 min)
- Blockers / decisions / escalation (remainder)

Top lines I want to get across:
- Perf regression baseline: we need a temporary mitigation that doesn’t require model downgrade (KV cache tuning or routing tweak). Don’t want to surface as "we downgraded models" to customers.
- Console rollout: we should be able to toggle UI change for new rollout path and still keep old flow for enterprise customers until we validate.
- Dedicated: Sales asked for a short lead-time guarantee for Q2 customers — need eng commitment for fast-turn capacity increases (what’s realistic?).

Notes to self / facts to confirm before the 1:1:
- SLO hit: latency p95 increased from 180ms -> 310ms across mixed-traffic profile last Thursday. Confirmed in Dashboard (trace ids in slack thread).
- Root cause suspicion: KV cache invalidation was pushed in prod with new batching heuristics; suspect fewer cache hits for prefix-heavy workloads.
- Rollback cost: reverting cache change is a ~2hr dev + 30m deploy, possible but status quo impact on new batching improvements.
- Canary numbers for console feature flag: 4% of orgs, 2 customer-reported regressions (UI hang on large orgs). Canary raw metrics attached in linked artifacts.

Questions I want to ask the ENG lead:
1) If I ask for a quick toggle to pin routing to stable backend (disable new cache heuristics) for hosted API for the next 24–48h, can we do it without a full rollback? Quick answer: yes/no + estimated time.
2) For console canary errors, do we have an immediate mitigation that doesn't need a rollback (server-side rate limit tweak or client-side debounce)?
3) Dedicated capacity: what is the fastest we can add + verify an extra rack/pool for a committed customer? Steps and risks.
4) Private onboarding: what are the recurring delays we see on customer network validations? Who owns each step (security checklist vs infra vs solutions)?

Proposed asks / what I will request:
- Action A: Temporary backend toggle for hosted API cache heuristics. Owner: Eng (TBD). Target: within 6h after decision.
- Action B: Console feature-flag pause for customers > 500 seats until we patch UI hang. Owner: Product + Eng. Target: EOD today.
- Action C: Dedicated capacity playbook doc: ask SRE to draft 30/60/90 min steps and testing checklist. Owner: Eng infra + SRE. Target: EOW.
- Action D: Private onboarding heatmap: list top 5 recurring blockers from last 6 onboardings. Owner: Solutions Eng (Samira) + Eng. Target: next Tue sync.

Potential trade-offs to highlight:
- Toggling cache heuristics regresses token-cost improvements from batching; if we toggle, we should plan a short-term cost buffer and announce to finance.
- Pausing the console rollout slows UX improvements for smaller orgs but reduces enterprise risk.

Immediate follow-ups I’ll volunteer for in the meeting:
- Draft an email to affected customers summarizing mitigation steps (I can write the first draft).
- Coordinate with Sales to shortlist customers for targeted outreach if we toggle backend.
- Create a lightweight QA checklist for console canary to hand to SRE on call.

Parking lot (async items / not for 1:1 unless time):
- Longer-term: revisit batching strategy and KV eviction policy — need a small spike (2wk) to evaluate alternatives.
- Instrumentation gap: we still lack prefix-level cache hit breakdowns per tenant — ask observability team for a small dashboard.
- Consider a canary expansion criterion that includes org size and request distribution, not just traffic percent.

Draft action-item table (I’ll capture in linear after the meeting):
- Toggle cache heuristics (ask): Owner: Eng infra. ETA: 6h. Blockers: change review + deploy windows.
- Pause console flag for >500 seats: Owner: Product + Eng. ETA: EOD. Blockers: flagging logic + rollout automation.
- Dedicated capacity playbook: Owner: SRE + Infra. ETA: EOW. Blockers: validation harness + perf tests.
- Private onboarding heatmap: Owner: Solutions Eng. ETA: next Tue. Blockers: data export from CRM + de-identified logs.

Prep: brief notes I will say verbally (short):
- "We hit a perf regression; I want a short-term mitigation that avoids model downgrade and keeps customers unaffected while we root-cause. Can you give me a realistic surface area and timeline for a toggle?"
- "Console canary is showing an edge-case UI hang. We should stop expanding until we have a hotfix or a simple client throttle. What's the quickest safe step?"
- "For Dedicated deployments, Sales is expecting faster ramp. Can we agree a playbook by EOW that we can defend to customers?"

Open risks I want Eng to call out:
- If we toggle heuristics, latency improves but per-token cost might spike ~7–12% for worst-case workloads. Need finance sign-off for buffer.
- Hotfix for console may introduce regressions in older browser support — need cross-browser QA window.

Things to capture in notes during meeting:
- Exact commit/release ids referenced for the cache change.
- Whom ENG assigns as action owner for each ask and clear ETA.
- Any decision to roll back vs toggle and rationale.

Post-meeting quick checklist (once action owners assigned):
- Add tickets for each action in Linear and link to this doc.
- Update customers page & status page if we toggle any infra.
- Send short sync email to Sales + Customer Success with next steps and who they should contact.

Random scratch thoughts (keep for myself):
- Would be nice to have a midday "safety window" for toggles that minimally impacts customers but allows quick rollbacks. Maybe a small dedicated pool we can switch routing to for 24–48h.
- Consider adding a field in console feature-flagging UI to mark "enterprise-sensitive" so rollouts exclude orgs above threshold automatically.

End — aim to leave meeting with 3 confirmed owners + ETAs.

-- Ryan
